l: lust and sin, The Letter from James
s: Lust and sin form a progression in James 1: one's own lust draws away and entices the tempted person, conceives and bears sin, and full-grown sin produces death; knowing good yet not doing it is also sin.

l: word of truth, The Letter from James
s: The word of truth is the means by which God gave birth to believers as first fruits; the implanted word, received with humility, is able to save souls.

l: hearers and doers of the word, The Letter from James
s: In James chapter 1, readers are urged to be doers of the word, not merely hearers who deceive themselves. A mere hearer resembles someone who glimpses his face in a mirror and forgets it; one who looks into the perfect law of freedom and continues doing is blessed.

Religion, as James describes it in chapter 1, is worthless if someone fails to bridle his tongue and deceives his heart; pure, undefiled religion before God the Father is visiting fatherless and widows in affliction and staying unstained by the world.

Abraham is called 'our father', father of Isaac, and friend of God. He is declared righteous for believing God, and justified by works when he offered Isaac on the altar; his faith worked with his works and was perfected by them.
Rahab, a prostitute, is cited as a second example of someone justified by works: she received the messengers and sent them out another way.

l: rich man (with gold ring), The Letter from James
s: wears fine clothing The man with a gold ring and fine clothing is pictured coming into the synagogue and being given special attention and a good place to sit. The text also says that the rich oppress the readers, drag them before the courts, and blaspheme the honorable name by which they are called.

l: poor man (in filthy clothing), The Letter from James
s: wears filthy clothing The poor man in filthy clothing is pictured entering the synagogue and being told to stand there or sit by a footstool. The text says the readers have dishonored him, though God chose the poor to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom.

is sin [convicted by the law as transgressors] Partiality is forbidden in holding the faith of the Lord Jesus Christ and is shown in favoring the fine-clothed man over the poor man. It makes the readers judges with evil thoughts, is a sin, and convicts them by the law as transgressors.

l: royal law, The Letter from James
s: states love your neighbor as yourself [according to Scripture] The royal law is identified with the Scripture 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.' Fulfilling it is said to be doing well, while showing partiality breaks it and brings conviction as transgressors.

l: faith and works, The Letter from James
s: Faith and works is a teaching topic arguing that faith without works is dead. It begins with useless kind words to the hungry and the shuddering belief of demons, then cites Abraham, whose faith was perfected by works, concluding that people are justified by works, not faith alone.

The tongue is a little member that boasts great things, likened to a horse's bit, a ship's rudder, and a small fire spreading through a forest. It is a fire and world of iniquity that defiles the whole body, set aflame by Gehenna. No one can tame it; it is a restless evil full of deadly poison, both blessing God and cursing men.

l: blessing and cursing, The Letter from James
s: Blessing and cursing are said to come out of the same mouth, with the tongue blessing God and Father and cursing men made in God's image. The author says these things ought not to be so, comparing it to a spring that cannot send out both fresh and bitter water, a fig tree that cannot yield olives, or a vine that cannot yield figs.

l: earthly wisdom, The Letter from James
s: Earthly wisdom is rooted in bitter jealousy and selfish ambition, not from above; described as earthly, sensual, and demonic, it brings confusion and every evil deed wherever it appears.

l: wisdom from above, The Letter from James
s: Wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, free of partiality and hypocrisy; its righteous fruit is sown in peace by peacemakers.
has_relationship_to God [friendship with the world is hostility] Friendship with the world is declared hostility toward God. Whoever wants to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.

l: pleasures and wrong desires, The Letter from James
s: Pleasures warring in the readers' members are the source of wars and fightings among them; lust and coveting leave them lacking, and asking with wrong motives to spend on pleasures prevents receiving.

l: pride and humility, The Letter from James
s: God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble, according to the quoted Scripture. The readers are told to be subject to God and to humble themselves in the Lord's sight, and he will exalt them.

l: judging others, The Letter from James
s: A teaching on judging others: readers are told not to speak against or judge a brother, since that judges the law, making one a judge rather than a doer of it; only the one lawgiver can save and destroy, so no one may judge.

l: boasting about future plans, The Letter from James
s: is evil Those who say they will go to a city, spend a year, trade, and make a profit are rebuked for not knowing what tomorrow holds, since life is a vapor that appears briefly and vanishes. They ought to say 'If the Lord wills,' and their boasting is called evil.

l: laborers (who mowed the rich's fields), The Letter from James
s: is_owed withheld wages [kept back by fraud] The laborers who mowed the fields had their wages kept back by fraud. Their cries, along with those of the reapers, have entered the ears of the Lord of Armies.

has_state corroded [gold and silver; corrosion will testify against the rich] The riches of the oppressors are described as corrupted, with garments moth-eaten and gold and silver corroded. The corrosion will testify against them and eat their flesh like fire, since they laid up treasure in the last days.

l: withheld wages, The Letter from James
s: reaches Lord [cries enter the ears of the Lord of Armies] The wages of the laborers who mowed the fields were kept back by fraud. They cry out, and the cries have reached the Lord of Armies.

Patience is a virtue commanded until the Lord's coming; it is illustrated by the farmer awaiting the precious fruit, then by suffering prophets and Job's perseverance, with those who endured called blessed.

l: coming of the Lord, The Letter from James
s: has_status at hand The coming of the Lord is said to be at hand, and the believers are to be patient until it. The judge stands at the door, which is the reason given for not grumbling against one another.

Prayer is prescribed for the suffering and the sick, alongside the elders' anointing with oil in the Lord's name. Prayer of faith heals the sick and brings forgiveness; a righteous person's insistent prayer is powerfully effective, illustrated by Elijah praying for no rain, then rain.
